name: Cut Of Meat
tldr: 🥩 means steak or a premium dinner, often suggesting a steakhouse date, celebration, or treat.

contextMeanings.meaning: It directly identifies steak or another thick cut of meat being discussed, ordered, cooked, or photographed.
It stands in for an upscale meal, a steakhouse outing, or a generous treat without spelling out the plan.
It often works as a compact invitation to a nicer dinner or suggests that the sender wants to celebrate together.
contextMeanings.example: been thinking about that place you like... steak night? 🥩

contextMeanings.meaning: It can mark a team dinner, a meal involving clients, or an order from a steakhouse in workplace conversation.
contextMeanings.example: for the team lunch, should we order from the steakhouse? 🥩

platformNotes.note: In a private chat, 🥩 can carry an invitation more strongly than a public reaction. “Dinner tonight? 🥩” commonly reads as a simple plan for an upscale meal rather than just what the sender plans to eat.

On Instagram, 🥩 appears beside food photos, restaurant recommendations, and celebratory meal posts. Its meaning often comes from the caption, so it can be literal on a steak post and date-oriented in a couple's dinner story.

TikTok comments use 🥩 to react to restaurant clips, extravagant meals, or extravagant-looking food. In those fast exchanges it often adds excitement or mild disbelief rather than making a detailed dining plan.

In Slack, 🥩 is useful for a team lunch, dinner poll, or client-meeting plan. Because the emoji can sound more deliberate and expensive than an ordinary lunch, send the actual venue and budget when those details matter.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z often uses 🥩 as a playful shorthand for an extravagant meal or a fun night out. The exaggeration matters more than a literal request for steak.
Millennials frequently pair 🥩 with dinner plans, gifting, and date-night suggestions. Depending on the relationship, it can suggest generosity or a slightly more polished occasion.
Some Gen X users treat 🥩 more literally, especially around menus, groceries, and family meals. They may need a sentence such as “I mean steakhouse dinner” to confirm the invitation.

warnings.title: Too formal too early
warnings.description: In a new dating thread, 🥩 can make the invitation feel more deliberate and expensive than the relationship supports. Use 🍕, 🍻, or ☕ until a shared dinner feels comfortable.

warnings.title: Food does not match the mood
warnings.description: If a relationship or friendship has become casual, suddenly sending steak can feel like an attempt to revive a specific earlier mood. Name the occasion plainly or choose a more familiar food emoji.

seoDescription: What does 🥩 mean? It is shorthand for steak or a premium dinner, often used to suggest a steakhouse date, celebration, or treat.

longForm.overview:
🥩 began as a literal picture of steak or another thick cut of meat, and that food meaning is still its foundation. Before it became shorthand for an upscale meal, a dinner invitation, or “I'm treating you,” people sent it simply because steak was what they were talking about, what the photo showed, or what they wanted to eat. It can still work that way in a menu photo, a restaurant order, or a grocery list.

As a message on its own, however, 🥩 usually points toward a higher-priced meal. It often works as a compact invitation to a steakhouse, a celebratory dinner, or a romantic night out, rather than as a request for “any meat.” That is what separates it from plain food emojis: it adds a sense of occasion and expense. The joke is not that meat equals romance; it is that choosing steak says “I picked something a little more special than fast food.”
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
In a private chat, 🥩 often appears after someone proposes dinner, wants to celebrate good news, or signals that they are paying. “I got us a table 🥩” means a specific, probably nicer meal is happening. On social media, it can react to an elaborate steak dinner or an over-the-top food video, adding amused approval without a full sentence.

It also appears in restaurant conversations when the sender is narrowing down the plan: steakhouse, sushi, or a casual place. A single 🥩 is usually enough when both people already understand the occasion. If there is no shared context, the emoji may simply mean meat and leave the recipient guessing whether this is an invitation, a food choice, or a reaction.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
🥩 is risky in a new dating thread when the two people have not yet established a rhythm of meals together. It can feel like over-investing when the recipient was expecting something ordinary, so 🍕, 🍻, or ☕ may be a safer opening. The same emoji can also feel overly polished in a casual friendship or after a relationship has settled into a more relaxed pattern.

Do not use it as a substitute for discussing dietary needs, budgets, or an actual order. A steakhouse plan still needs a restaurant, a time, and enough information for everyone to participate. In a professional channel, keep the emoji beside a clear plan rather than relying on it to carry the whole message. If the occasion is small, use a simpler food emoji instead of making 🥩 carry more weight than intended.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🥩 as an invitation, answer the plan directly: propose a restaurant, suggest a time, or ask which steakhouse they mean. “yes, but you're paying first 🥩” can match a playful treat message, while “what time?” keeps the invitation moving without overthinking it.

If it reacts to your own food post or restaurant idea, acknowledge the recommendation and say whether you want to try it. When the emoji lands too formal, ask “are we celebrating?” or offer a casual option instead of ignoring it. That gives the sender an easy way to explain the occasion without forcing either person to guess.

faqs.question: What does 🥩 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: On its own, 🥩 can mean steak or a premium dinner. From someone interested in you, it may be a subtle invitation to eat out, but it is not automatically romantic or flirty.

faqs.question: Is 🥩 flirty?
faqs.answer: It can be, especially in a dating thread where steak represents a pricier dinner or a treat. The same emoji is often just about food, so the surrounding message decides which meaning applies.

faqs.question: What does 🥩 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it often reacts to an extravagant meal, restaurant clip, or food that looks excessive. It may mean “that looks amazing” rather than proposing an actual dinner.

faqs.question: Is 🥩 appropriate for a first date?
faqs.answer: It can make a first-date meal plan feel more formal or expensive than intended. A casual food or drink emoji is usually easier until you know the other person shares that preference.

conversationExamples.message: that steak place we saved looks unreal, want to go friday? 🥩
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a dinner invitation with a slightly premium tone. Reply with a day and time, but do not assume the meal has to be expensive.

conversationExamples.message: i got paid today, steak's on me saturday 🥩
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is offering to treat the group to a nicer meal. Ask where you are eating and whether anyone has dietary restrictions.

conversationExamples.message: should i book a table for the client dinner? steakhouse was mentioned 🥩
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is literal planning rather than slang. Confirm the venue, attendees, budget, and reservation details.

conversationExamples.message: mom asked what we're having for dinner and i only sent this 🥩
conversationExamples.interpretation: The family member used the emoji as a literal answer about meat. Clarify whether they meant steak, what kind, and how it fits into the meal.

conversationExamples.message: that steak looked twice the size of my plate for the same money 😭🥩
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here 🥩 reacts to an extravagant or unfair food video. Respond to the visual joke rather than treating it as a dining invitation.
